claims.says: Lexicographic list comparison, shorter list first on a common prefix, is transitive on lists whose elements satisfy P when the element comparator is antisymmetric and transitive on P.
If an element comparator is antisymmetric and transitive, the lexicographic list comparison built from it, as in Rust's slice cmp, is antisymmetric and transitive too.
Comparing by a lawful key and breaking ties with a second comparator, as Rust's Ordering::then does, is transitive when the second comparator is transitive on triples whose keys tie.
The lexicographic comparison of (Nat, Int, Nat) triples used as the float position key is antisymmetric and transitive.
Two's-complement wrapping onto the i64 range leaves every integer that already fits in i64 unchanged.
